name: Can townhome construction be phased by unit?

mainEntity.name: Can a townhome development in Los Angeles be built in phases, or does it need to be completed all at once?
mainEntity.text: Can a townhome development in Los Angeles be built in phases, or does it need to be completed all at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: Phasing can help reduce financing pressure, but it is not always practical or allowed as planned. A phased townhome project must still maintain safe access, utility service, drainage, and construction logistics throughout each stage. If later phases depend on temporary systems or unfinished common areas, approvals can become more difficult. Phasing also affects sales strategy, because completed units may need to coexist with active construction. The feasibility of phasing should be studied before permits are submitted so the overall plan accounts for fire access, grading, staging, and temporary circulation. In some cases, a project is better built all at once because the cost of mobilization, temporary infrastructure, and repeated inspections outweighs any savings from splitting the work. A design-build team can help determine whether phasing improves cash flow or simply adds complexity.
acceptedAnswer.description: Townhome projects can sometimes be phased, but phasing depends on site access, approvals, utility sequencing, and how the development is permitted. Phasing is easier when each stage can function safely and independently.
